Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.



We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/culture and learn more about how we work https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/careers.



About the team

The Internal Controls team plays a critical role in adhering to controls frameworks and creating space for risk mitigation and oversight. We want to ensure that Wealthsimple maintains a secure operational environment by implementing, monitoring and testing controls designed to safeguard assets, keep our reporting accurate, and make our processes more efficient.



About the role

We are looking to expand our team with a Manager, Internal Controls to help build and run our internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR) program. This role will be instrumental in ensuring Wealthsimple meets its regulatory obligations while building a scalable compliance function.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Internal Controls, the successful candidate will build and shape internal controls around the processes we already have and build the control framework for new products as we launch them. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role — you'll own the control framework and documentation, direct testing, and work with the control owners across Finance, Operations and Engineering who run the controls, so that they are designed, implemented and operating effectively.

 

What you’ll do

 - Be a strong voice within the Finance team and across Wealthsimple by proactively shaping effective and efficient controls around existing processes as well as designing an effective control framework for new products;

 - Work alongside our external advisors to build out the ICFR program, then own the process narratives, RCMs, flowcharts and test procedures and keep them current;

 - Plan and direct walkthroughs and testing against the annual ICFR plan, whether testing is done in house or by a co-source firm, and support control owners as they remediate deficiencies;

 - Serve as the primary point of contact for external auditors, coordinating evidence requests, walkthroughs, and finding remediation. Coordinate testing activities to ensure deadlines are met with high quality outputs for:
   
   - Financial reporting audits for all entities;
   
   - SOC 1 audits;
   
   - Other audits requiring control work as they arise;

 - Proactively work with internal stakeholders to determine the impact of business decisions on the financial processes, operations and engineering; and

 - Work with technology to develop best-in-class controls documentation and solutions including AI-enabled tooling.
   
   

Skills you bring

 - 5+ years in internal controls or audit, with hands-on ICFR experience under SOX or CSOX, working knowledge of COSO 2013, and a CPA designation or equivalent;

 - Experience working in SOX or CSOX control environment in a public company

 - Hands-on experience using technology — including AI tools — to document, test, or automate controls
   
   

Nice to have

 - Experience building an ICFR program, or substantially expanding one

 - Experience in financial services, ideally brokerage, banking or payments

 - Experience supporting SOC 1 Type 2 audit

 - Experience working with Optro (formerly AuditBoard)

 - Exposure to a high-growth fintech or technology company



Who you are 

 - You bring people along — you can explain why a strong control environment matters and build/promote awareness across the organization

 About the Role 
 McKesson is seeking a Sr. Vendor & Operations Lead to lead vendor governance and service operations coordination across the Human Capital Management (HCM) technology portfolio, supporting HR, Payroll, Time & Attendance, Total Rewards, Talent, and related integrations. 
 This role establishes operational governance processes, manages vendor commitments and commercial obligations, coordinates financial planning and contract renewals, and drives timely closure of service risks and corrective actions. Working closely with HCM Solution Managers, Technical Delivery Leads, Architects, Project Managers, and enterprise partners, this role strengthens service reliability, operational transparency, cost management, and vendor accountability.   
The successful candidate will serve as the central point of coordination for HCM vendor performance, operational readiness, governance reporting, financial oversight, and action management. This role is accountable for driving follow-through, ensuring commitments are completed, risks are escalated, and operational outcomes are achieved. 
 Success in this role depends on ensuring vendor commitments are actively managed, operational risks are addressed, and actions are driven to closure. This role is accountable for operational follow-through and escalation management rather than technical execution or business-process ownership. 
 What You'll Do 
 HCM Service Operations & Governance 
 Establish and lead a recurring HCM operational governance cadence across supported vendors and service providers.   
 Consolidate service health, risks, vendor commitments, decisions, corrective actions, and escalations into a single operational view.   
 Develop operational reporting focused on service outcomes, accountability, emerging risks, and business impact.   
 Facilitate governance forums and ensure actions and commitments are actively tracked through completion.   
 Prepare and present operational reporting to leadership and stakeholders.   
 AMS Service Accountability   
 Govern Application Management Services (AMS) commitments and performance.   
 Monitor:   
 Service coverage   
 Resource capacity   
 Backlog aging   
 Open defects   
 Recurring incidents   
 SLA attainment   
 Problem management activities   
 Corrective-action completion   
 Validate vendor-reported metrics against operational performance data and agreed service-management standards.   
 Partner with HCM stakeholders to identify service gaps and continuous improvement opportunities.   
 Business-Critical Calendar & Service Readiness   
 Coordinate vendor support readiness for:   
 Payroll processing   
 Time collection   
 Benefits enrollment   
 Open enrollment cycles   
 Compensation planning cycles   
 Year-end processing   
 Major platform releases   
 Ensure escalation procedures, support coverage models, and contingency plans are documented and operationally ready.   
 Maintain awareness of critical HCM business calendars and coordinate vendor preparedness accordingly.   
 Renewal & Contract Readiness   
 Maintain an integrated contract and renewal calendar covering:   
 Notice periods   
 Auto-renewal provisions   
 Licensing assumptions   
 Service changes   
 Renewal milestones   
 Approval timelines   
 Accountable stakeholders   
 Lead HCM requirements and commercial-readiness coordination in partnership with Procurement and Legal.   
 Coordinate renewal reviews with Procurement, Legal, Finance, HR, and Technology stakeholders.   
 Support sourcing and commercial discussions through operational requirements, service-performance data, stakeholder alignment, and business priorities.   
 Financial Operations   
 Coordinate vendor spend forecasting and budget planning activities.   
 Support invoice validation, purchase-order management, accrual planning, and variance analysis.   
 Partner with Finance to improve financial transparency, spending accuracy, and forecasting reliability.   
 Reconcile vendor costs against approved scope, contractual obligations, approved changes, and licensing assumptions.   
 Monitor financial commitments and identify opportunities for cost optimization.   
 Escalation & Action Closure   
 Coordinate cross-functional and cross-vendor escalations.   
 Maintain ownership tracking, due dates, action logs, and risk registers.   
 Verify closure with accountable service owners, technical leads, and stakeholders.   
 Escalate unresolved business-impacting issues with recommended options and decision support.   
 Ensure corrective actions, remediation plans, and vendor commitments progress to verified completion.   
 Service Transition & Continuity   
 Coordinate operational readiness reviews for:   
 New implementations   
 Vendor transitions   
 Acquisitions   
 Divestitures   
 Managed-service transitions   
 Ensure support ownership, documentation, knowledge transfer, service coverage, training, and acceptance criteria are completed prior to transition.   
 Partner with service owners and delivery teams to ensure long-term operational sustainability.   
 Controls & Third-Party Risk   
 Coordinate vendor-related audit evidence requests and compliance activities.   
 Support third-party risk management reviews and remediation efforts.   
 Coordinate access-review activities with Security and designated control owners.   
 Maintain continuity and vendor governance documentation.   
 Track compliance, audit, and risk-mitigation actions through successful completion.   
 Accountability for Follow-Through   
 Drive completion of vendor commitments, remediation plans, action items, and operational improvements.   
 Proactively manage overdue actions and unresolved risks.   
 Escalate stalled progress with clear recommendations and decision options.   
 Ensure governance forums result in measurable outcomes rather than status reporting alone.   
 Basic Requirements   
 Education & Experience   
 Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.   
 7+ years of experience in vendor management, service delivery, operations management, governance, supplier management, technology operations, or related disciplines.   
 Experience governing enterprise HCM SaaS platforms and managed application services.   
 Experience supporting HR Technology, Payroll, Time & Attendance, Benefits, Talent, or Workforce Management environments.   
 Experience managing vendor performance, corrective-action plans, operational governance programs, and service reviews.   
 Experience coordinating cross-functional stakeholders in large enterprise environments.   
Functional Expertise   
 Understanding of payroll and time-and-attendance service criticality, sensitive employee data, and business-cycle dependencies.   
 Experience with IT Service Management (ITSM), including:   
 Incident Management   
 Problem Management   
 Change Management   
 Service Transition   
 Operational Governance   
 Experience translating contracts and statements of work into measurable service obligations, financial controls, operational reporting, and vendor accountability measures.   
 Experience managing SLAs, KPIs, scorecards, and service-performance metrics.   
 Experience supporting operational readiness, business continuity, and risk-management activities.   
Leadership & Collaboration   
 Strong communication, executive presentation, and stakeholder management skills.   
 Ability to coordinate across HR, Payroll, Technology, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Security, and external vendors without direct reporting authority.   
 Demonstrated ability to drive accountability, influence outcomes, and achieve closure through collaboration.   
Preferred Skills/Experience   
 Familiarity with Workday, ADP, UKG, Oracle HCM, SAP SuccessFactors, Ceridian, or similar enterprise HCM platforms.   
 Experience supporting HCM managed-service providers and AMS engagements.   
 Experience in highly regulated or compliance-focused environments.   
 ITIL Foundation or related service-management certification.   
 Experience supporting enterprise-scale vendor ecosystems and outsourced technology services.   
 What Success Looks Like   
 Success in this role is demonstrated when:   
 Renewals and contract notice periods are managed proactively without avoidable last-minute escalations.   
 Vendor commitments and corrective actions have documented owners, target dates, and verified closure.   
 Service reporting reflects business outcomes and operational impact, not solely vendor-reported SLA attainment.   
 Vendor spend, invoices, forecasts, and obligations are transparent, accurate, and traceable to approved scope.   
 Payroll, benefits, compensation, and other critical HCM cycles have documented support readiness, escalation coverage, and operational continuity plans.   
 Governance forums consistently drive accountability, risk mitigation, and service improvement.   
 Vendor-related risks, audit findings, and operational issues are resolved in a timely manner.   
 Routine vendor coordination and operational follow-through no longer require leadership intervention.

 About the role 
 We are looking for a Senior Data Developer (Engineer) to help establish the data foundation for Contact Distributor, Intact’s new platform for broker and distributor master data. The platform will replace fragmented legacy sources including the Halcion and Classic mainframes, Microsoft Access databases and Excel-based tools with a trusted, governed view of brokerages, broker codes and organizational hierarchies.
 As a key member of the initial product squad, you will play a hands-on role in profiling, cleansing, migrating and integrating legacy data. You will also help embed data quality, governance and operational reliability into the product from day one. You will work in a self-managed, cross-functional product team alongside a Tech Lead, software engineers, architects, business experts and a Product Owner.
 The ideal candidate is a hands-on senior data engineer who can independently design, build and operate production-grade data pipelines. You are comfortable working with incomplete information, validating assumptions against real data, taking ownership from discovery through production support, and challenging decisions constructively. You bring ideas forward and collaborate effectively with both technical and business stakeholders.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Data Modeling: Co-design and implement the target data model with the Data Architect: multi-level hierarchies, effective dating and history, audit/versioning, and legacy-to-golden-record crosswalks. Validate the model against real legacy data rather than assumptions. 
 ETL / ELT Development: Design, build and operate batch and incremental ETL/ELT pipelines on AWS, from mainframe extracts, flat files and databases into a layered data lake (raw, standardized, curated). Make pipelines config-driven, so a new source means new configuration, not new code. Build them to be restartable, idempotent and monitored, with clear error handling, orchestration and scheduling. 
 Data Migration: Lead extraction, profiling, cleansing, normalization, match/merge and reconciliation through parallel run and cutover. 
 Data Quality & Governance: Turn business rules into automated data quality controls. Ensure lineage, cataloging, security and cost control across pipelines. 
 Integration: Publish trusted data to downstream consumers, such as EDP for reporting and legacy systems through file-based backfeeds, working closely with the Java backend team. 
 Quality & DevOps: Implement unit, integration and automated data tests. Apply CI/CD and Infrastructure as Code principles, in line with security and governance standards. 
 Leadership & Collaboration: Provide technical guidance, promote best practices (code reviews, standards, tests, documentation), and challenge decisions with evidence from real data. Contribute to design discussions and sprint planning, and communicate effectively with the Product Owner and stakeholders in a Scrum/Kanban product culture focused on incremental delivery.

 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field. 
 8+ years of experience in data engineering / software engineering, including 3+ years in a senior or lead role. 
 Proven experience designing, building and running production ETL/ELT pipelines at scale (batch and incremental loads, orchestration, scheduling, error handling and recovery), whether code-based or with ETL tools. 
 Demonstrated experience migrating data from legacy/mainframe or packaged systems (extraction, cleansing, normalization, reconciliation, dual-run/cutover). 
 Excellent SQL and relational data modeling skills (hierarchies, historization), including performance tuning. 
 Strong programming skills in Python or Java for data pipelines, plus AWS ecosystem. 
 Solid understanding of CI/CD, version control (Git), automated data testing and observability. 
 Demonstrated initiative and leadership: able to challenge, influence and bring others along. 
 No Canadian work experience is required; however, candidates must be authorized to work in Canada. 
 For candidates located in Quebec, bilingualism in French and English is required due to frequent collaboration with English-speaking colleagues across Canada.

 Experience with AWS data services (Glue, EMR, Step Functions, Athena) and Spark (PySpark or Java/Scala). 
 Experience with ETL/integration tools (e.g. Informatica, Talend, DataStage, SSIS) and enterprise schedulers (e.g. Control-M). 
 Change data capture (CDC) or event-driven integration experience. 
 Knowledge of Master Data Management concepts (golden record, survivorship, reference data). 
 Experience with Databricks or Snowflake.
